Brick and Concrete Disposal Guide

Whether you’re finishing a renovation, clearing a demolition site, or just getting rid of a few leftover bricks, figuring out the best way to dispose of brick and concrete can feel like a puzzle. In this guide we’ll walk you through your options, share DIY tips, and explain when it makes sense to call in the pros—like 1-800-GOT-JUNK?—so you can keep your project on track and your wallet happy.

Why Proper Disposal Matters

Brick and concrete are heavy, bulky, and not always welcome at the local landfill. Mishandling them can lead to:

  • Unnecessary fines from your municipality.
  • Damage to your vehicle or property during transport.
  • Environmental impact from sending recyclable material to landfill.

By taking the right steps, you protect the environment, avoid penalties, and often save money.

Your Disposal Options

1. Reuse on Your Property

If you have a garden, driveway, or patio project in mind, reclaimed bricks can become a charming pathway, while crushed concrete makes an excellent base for new pavers. This “reuse” route is the most cost‑effective, but it requires some planning and labor.

2. Local Recycling Centers

Many cities operate facilities that crush concrete into aggregate and sort bricks for reuse. Call your municipality to learn about drop‑off locations, accepted quantities, and any associated fees.

3. Bulk Waste Pickup Services

Some towns offer scheduled bulk‑waste days where you can leave large items like bricks and concrete at the curb. Check the schedule and any weight limits to ensure compliance.

4. Professional Junk Removal

When you have a lot of material, limited space, or simply don’t want to lift a 2‑ton load yourself, a junk‑removal service can handle the heavy lifting. Companies like 1-800-GOT-JUNK? specialize in safely loading, hauling, and disposing of construction debris.

DIY Disposal Tips: How to Do It Yourself (Safely)

Gather the Right Tools

  • Heavy‑duty dolly or hand truck: Makes moving pallets of bricks easier.
  • Shovel and wheelbarrow: Ideal for scooping broken concrete.
  • Protective gear: Gloves, steel‑toe boots, and safety glasses.

Break It Down

Large concrete slabs are easier to handle once they’re broken into smaller pieces (no larger than 12‑inch chunks). Use a sledgehammer or a concrete breaker to reduce the weight per item.

Maximize Space

Stack bricks on their widest side and interlock them like a brick wall. For concrete, pile crushed pieces in a conical shape to keep the load stable.

Load the Truck Correctly

Place the heaviest items (usually concrete) at the bottom of the truck, then layer bricks on top. Secure the load with strap ties to prevent shifting during transit.

Know Your Local Regulations

Many jurisdictions require a permit for more than a certain number of bricks or a specific volume of concrete. A quick call to your city’s public works department can save you from surprise fines.

When to Call the Professionals

Even the most seasoned DIYer will hit a roadblock when:

  • Volume is high: More than a cubic yard of material can quickly become a logistical nightmare.
  • Space is limited: If you can’t fit the debris on your driveway or curb, a professional service can bring a larger truck.
  • Time is tight: Need the site cleared for the next phase of construction? A junk‑removal crew can show up the same day.

That’s where 1-800-GOT-JUNK? shines. Their trained teams handle everything from loading to disposal, allowing you to focus on the project at hand.

Cost Factors & How to Save Money

What Influences the Price?

  • Weight and volume: Most services charge by the load size or by the ton.
  • Location: Urban areas may have higher disposal fees than rural zones.
  • Recycling vs. landfill: Materials that can be recycled often cost less to dispose of.

Tips to Keep Costs Down

  1. Separate materials: Keep bricks away from concrete if possible; recycling centers often price them differently.
  2. Compress the load: Smaller, denser loads reduce the number of trips required.
  3. Schedule a single pick‑up: Consolidating multiple small jobs into one service call saves on labor.
  4. Ask about discounts: Some junk‑removal companies offer promotional rates for first‑time customers.

Even with these DIY savings, the convenience factor of a professional service can outweigh the extra cost—especially when you factor in the time and effort saved.

Final Checklist Before You Start

  • ✅ Verify local disposal rules and any required permits.
  • ✅ Decide whether you’ll reuse, recycle, or hire a removal service.
  • ✅ Gather safety gear and appropriate moving equipment.
  • ✅ Break large concrete pieces into manageable sizes.
  • ✅ Load and secure the material properly in your vehicle.
  • ✅ Contact 1-800-GOT-JUNK? if the job exceeds your capacity.

By following this guide, you’ll navigate brick and concrete disposal with confidence, protect the environment, and keep your project moving forward. Remember, whether you choose to DIY or let the experts handle it, the key is to stay organized, stay safe, and stay informed.
